title: Raft Log Compaction, InstallSnapshot RPC & WAL Truncation

spark.summary: Periodic Copy-on-Write snapshotting at (lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm), O(1) WAL prefix truncation, and chunked InstallSnapshot RPCs bound Raft disk growth and cut follower recovery from 4+ hours to under 45 seconds.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never freeze the state machine during snapshotting or stream unthrottled gigabyte snapshots; fork a Copy-on-Write checkpoint, retain a small suffix log for mildly lagging followers, and stream InstallSnapshot chunks with rate limiting.
spark.byteSummary:
At 50,000+ mutations/sec (common in etcd, CockroachDB, or Kafka KRaft), an uncompacted Raft Write-Ahead Log (WAL) balloons to 500 GB in days. Restarting a node forces it to replay 1B+ log entries for 4+ hours while missed heartbeats trigger spurious leader election storms.

Raft log compaction replaces the committed log prefix [1..lastIncludedIndex] with a point-in-time Snapshot of the state machine tagged with `(lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm)` and optional cluster membership configuration. The node atomically writes the snapshot, fsyncs it, and discards the compacted WAL prefix while retaining a small suffix log.

When a follower lags behind `leader.firstLogIndex` (so `nextIndex < firstLogIndex`), the leader cannot catch it up with normal `AppendEntries` RPCs. Instead, the leader streams the latest snapshot in bounded chunks (`offset`, `data`, `done`) via `InstallSnapshot` RPCs, allowing the follower to atomically swap its state machine and immediately resume normal log replication.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: Why Unbounded Raft Logs Fail at 50K Writes/Sec
learningJourney.purpose: Quantify WAL growth, recovery replay latency, and election-storm risks when Raft logs are never compacted.
learningJourney.explanation: Every committed mutation appends to the Raft WAL. At 50,000 writes/sec (~800 bytes/entry), a cluster generates ~3.4 TB/day of raw log history—or 500 GB in just 3.5 hours. On node restart, replaying 1B+ entries through the state machine takes 4+ hours, starving reads and risking quorum loss.

sectionDiagram.title: 50K Writes/Sec Uncompacted WAL Growth & 4-Hour Replay Storm

cards.label: Redundant History
cards.detail: Overwriting the same key 10,000 times stores 10,000 log entries even though only 1 current value exists.

cards.label: Quorum Fragility
cards.detail: While one node spends 4 hours replaying WAL, losing a second node breaks Raft majority quorum.

sectionDiagram.summary: Unbounded Raft logs grow to 500 GB at 50K writes/sec, causing 4-hour recovery replays and quorum fragility.
sectionDiagram.caption: 50K writes/sec without compaction produces 500 GB WALs and 4-hour follower replay stalls.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: Snapshot Metadata & Atomic WAL Prefix Truncation
learningJourney.purpose: Define the Snapshot header (lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm) and safe prefix truncation invariants.
learningJourney.explanation: A Raft snapshot captures the deterministic state machine at a committed `lastIncludedIndex` and `lastIncludedTerm` (plus the latest cluster config). Only AFTER the snapshot file is durably fsynced and atomically renamed can the node truncate WAL segments strictly below `lastIncludedIndex`, preserving `prevLogIndex`/`prevLogTerm` continuity.

sectionDiagram.title: Durable Snapshot Commit Before WAL Prefix Truncation

cards.label: Crash-Safety Ordering
cards.detail: Truncating WAL before fsyncing the snapshot risks losing committed state if power fails mid-compaction.

cards.label: Suffix Retention
cards.detail: Keeping a small suffix (e.g. 10K entries) avoids InstallSnapshot for followers that only paused briefly.

sectionDiagram.summary: Nodes must fsync and atomically rename the snapshot before unlinking older WAL segments while keeping a small suffix.
sectionDiagram.caption: Snapshot metadata (lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm) is fsynced before truncating old WAL segments.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: Copy-on-Write & RocksDB Checkpoint Snapshotting
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate stop-the-world state machine freezes during gigabyte snapshot serialization.
learningJourney.explanation: Locking an in-memory map to serialize 20 GB of KV state stalls Raft apply threads for minutes and triggers election timeouts. Instead, in-memory engines use `fork()` Copy-on-Write (or persistent HAMT trees), while disk-backed engines (etcd/RocksDB) create an instant `hard-link` Checkpoint/MVCC read snapshot in < 1 ms and stream it asynchronously.

sectionDiagram.title: Zero-Freeze Snapshotting via RocksDB Checkpoints & CoW

cards.label: Sub-Millisecond Pause
cards.detail: Hard-linking immutable RocksDB SSTables takes < 1 ms regardless of whether the DB is 5 GB or 500 GB.

cards.label: Checksumming
cards.detail: Always attach per-chunk CRC32C or SHA-256 checksums to detect silent bit-rot during snapshot transfer.

sectionDiagram.summary: RocksDB hard-link checkpoints and Copy-on-Write clones decouple gigabyte snapshot I/O from the live Raft apply loop.
sectionDiagram.caption: O(1) RocksDB checkpoints and CoW forks let background workers stream snapshots with zero apply-loop stalls.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: Detecting Lagging Followers & InstallSnapshot RPC
learningJourney.purpose: Handle followers whose nextIndex falls behind the leader's compacted firstLogIndex.
learningJourney.explanation: When a restarted or newly added follower has `nextIndex < leader.firstLogIndex`, the leader no longer holds the log entries needed for `AppendEntries`. The leader switches that peer's replication state to `StateSnapshot` and streams `InstallSnapshot(term, leaderId, lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm, offset, data[], done)` chunks.

sectionDiagram.title: Switching from AppendEntries to Chunked InstallSnapshot RPC

cards.label: Idempotent Offsets
cards.detail: Streaming fixed-size chunks (e.g., 1-4 MB) with explicit byte offsets lets followers recover cleanly from transient network drops.

cards.label: Term Guard
cards.detail: Followers reject any InstallSnapshot RPC with term < currentTerm, preserving Raft leader safety.

sectionDiagram.summary: Leaders switch lagging followers to chunked InstallSnapshot RPCs when nextIndex < firstLogIndex, then resume AppendEntries.
sectionDiagram.caption: When nextIndex < firstLogIndex, the leader streams InstallSnapshot chunks before resetting nextIndex to resume AppendEntries.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Follower Atomic State-Machine Swap & Suffix Replay
learningJourney.purpose: Apply an incoming snapshot safely on a follower without corrupting local state if a crash occurs mid-transfer.
learningJourney.explanation: A follower writes incoming `InstallSnapshot` chunks to a temporary staging file (`snapshot.tmp`). Only when `done == true` and checksums pass does it fsync, atomically rename the snapshot, discard any conflicting log entries up to `lastIncludedIndex`, reload its state machine from the snapshot, and ACK the leader.

sectionDiagram.title: Crash-Safe Follower Snapshot Staging & Atomic Reload

cards.label: Sub-45s Recovery
cards.detail: Transferring a compacted 4 GB snapshot at 1 Gbps takes ~32 seconds—vs. 4+ hours replaying 1B WAL entries.

cards.label: Preserve Newer Suffix
cards.detail: If the follower's log already matches (lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm), retain entries after lastIncludedIndex.

sectionDiagram.summary: Followers stage InstallSnapshot chunks in a temp file, verify checksums, atomically swap state on done=true, and recover in < 45 seconds.
sectionDiagram.caption: Followers stage chunks in snapshot.tmp, verify CRC32C on done=true, and atomically swap state for < 45s recovery.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: Rate-Limiting Snapshot Streams & Heartbeat Isolation
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent multi-gigabyte snapshot transfers from saturating NICs and causing heartbeat election timeouts.
learningJourney.explanation: If a leader blasts a 20 GB snapshot to two restarting followers at full 10 Gbps line rate, NIC saturation and TCP queue bloat can delay Raft `AppendEntries` heartbeats past `electionTimeout` (e.g., 150-500 ms), triggering split-brain elections. Production clusters separate heartbeat RPCs onto a high-priority QoS/transport channel and token-bucket rate-limit `InstallSnapshot` streams.

sectionDiagram.title: Token-Bucket Snapshot Throttling & Dedicated Heartbeat Lane

cards.label: Heartbeat Priority
cards.detail: Dedicated connections for AppendEntries heartbeats prevent head-of-line blocking behind 4 MB snapshot chunks.

cards.label: PreVote Extension
cards.detail: PreVote prevents a briefly congested node from incrementing cluster terms and disrupting the active leader.

sectionDiagram.summary: Dedicated heartbeat connections, token-bucket snapshot throttling, and PreVote prevent election storms during follower rebuilds.
sectionDiagram.caption: Priority heartbeat lanes, token-bucket snapshot caps, and PreVote prevent election storms during recovery.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Compaction Triggers, ReadIndex & Quorum Safety
learningJourney.purpose: Choose snapshot thresholds (entry count vs. WAL bytes) and preserve linearizable ReadIndex across compactions.
learningJourney.explanation: Triggering snapshots solely by entry count (e.g., every 100K entries) can snapshot too often on tiny writes or too rarely on large 1 MB values. Dual triggers (`entries >= 100K OR wal_bytes >= 256 MB`) keep disk bounded predictably, while jittering thresholds across peers prevents all 3-5 replicas from compacting simultaneously.

sectionDiagram.title: Jittered Dual Triggers & Concurrent Quorum Stability

cards.label: Anti-Herd Jitter
cards.detail: Jittering compaction thresholds by +/-15% ensures only one replica compacts at a time, preserving write P99.

cards.label: ReadIndex Continuity
cards.detail: Snapshots never roll back commitIndex, so ReadIndex linearizability remains unbroken.

sectionDiagram.summary: Jittered dual triggers (entries OR WAL bytes) bound both disk usage and replay time without synchronized replica pauses.
sectionDiagram.caption: Jittered dual triggers (100K entries or 256 MB WAL) stagger replica compactions while preserving ReadIndex safety.

knowledgeChecks.question: When must a Raft leader send an `InstallSnapshot` RPC instead of `AppendEntries` to a lagging follower?

options.text: Whenever the follower's `nextIndex` is strictly less than the leader's compacted `firstLogIndex`.
options.feedback: Correct. Because the leader already truncated log entries before firstLogIndex, only a snapshot can bridge the gap.

options.text: Whenever a single write payload exceeds 4 KB.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Normal AppendEntries handles arbitrary entry sizes as long as they are still in the leader's WAL.
Incorrect. InstallSnapshot is only for followers whose required log prefix was already compacted.

options.text: Only when the cluster has an even number of nodes.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Log compaction is independent of cluster parity.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: If follower.nextIndex < leader.firstLogIndex, the needed WAL entries no longer exist on the leader, requiring InstallSnapshot.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should Raft nodes use Copy-on-Write (CoW) or RocksDB hard-link checkpoints rather than locking the state machine during snapshotting?

options.text: Because locking the state machine to serialize gigabytes of data stalls the apply loop and triggers missed heartbeat election storms.
options.feedback: Correct. O(1) RocksDB checkpoints or CoW forks let background threads stream the snapshot with zero apply-loop stalls.

options.text: Because RocksDB checkpoints delete the Raft WAL automatically.
options.feedback: Incorrect. WAL truncation is still explicitly gated on fsyncing the snapshot.

options.text: Because CoW snapshots skip CRC32C checksums.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Checksums are still required for crash/transfer integrity.

options.text: Because CoW snapshots eliminate the need for `lastIncludedIndex`.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Every snapshot must record lastIncludedIndex and lastIncludedTerm.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Stop-the-world state-machine serialization causes multi-second/minute pauses that trigger Raft election timeouts; CoW/checkpoints avoid this.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do production Raft implementations retain a small WAL suffix (e.g., 10K entries) after creating a snapshot at `lastIncludedIndex`?

options.text: To allow briefly paused followers to catch up via fast `AppendEntries` instead of streaming a multi-gigabyte `InstallSnapshot`.
options.feedback: Correct. A small suffix absorbs minor network blips or GC pauses without triggering full snapshot transfers.

options.text: Because Raft forbids truncating more than 50% of the WAL.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Raft allows truncating all entries up to lastIncludedIndex; keeping a suffix is a performance optimization.
Incorrect. WAL segments store Raft log entries, not certificates.

options.text: To disable PreVote during leader elections.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Suffix retention is unrelated to PreVote.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Retaining a small suffix of recent WAL entries lets slightly behind followers catch up via lightweight AppendEntries.

beginner.summary: Raft log compaction periodically saves a compact snapshot of the current database state so nodes can delete old log history and recover in seconds instead of hours.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Saving a snapshot and streaming it in chunks to lagging followers prevents disks from filling up and keeps restarts fast.
beginner.byteSummary:
If a Raft cluster keeps every write forever in its log, disks fill up and restarted servers take hours to replay old history.

By periodically saving a snapshot of the current state and deleting older log entries, nodes stay small and recover in under a minute.

intermediate.summary: Pair Copy-on-Write / RocksDB checkpoints with fsync-before-truncate WAL pruning, suffix retention, and chunked `InstallSnapshot` RPCs.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Dual compaction triggers (100K entries or 256 MB WAL) and chunked `InstallSnapshot` cut recovery from 4+ hours to < 45 seconds.
intermediate.byteSummary:
At 50K writes/sec, uncompacted Raft WALs reach 500 GB and cause 4-hour replay storms. Using O(1) RocksDB checkpoints or CoW clones avoids locking the apply loop.

Once fsynced with `(lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm)`, older WAL segments are pruned (retaining a small suffix), and lagging followers catch up via chunked `InstallSnapshot` RPCs.

advanced.summary: Production engines add token-bucket `InstallSnapshot` rate limiting, priority heartbeat lanes, PreVote guards, and jittered dual triggers for sub-10ms write P99.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Isolating heartbeats from rate-limited snapshot streams and jittering replica compaction thresholds prevents split-brain election storms.
advanced.byteSummary:
Unthrottled multi-gigabyte `InstallSnapshot` transfers saturate NICs and starve `AppendEntries` heartbeats, causing spurious elections. Production clusters isolate heartbeats on priority connections, cap snapshot streams via token buckets, and enable PreVote.

Jittering dual triggers (`100K entries OR 256 MB WAL` +/-15%) prevents simultaneous replica stalls while preserving `ReadIndex` linearizability.
